A regional reference map with genuine, dated satellite detections. Singapore station wind does not establish regional smoke movement. See ASMC for the latest haze assessment.

Loading dated snapshot…

Snapshot from NASA’s rolling 24-hour Southeast Asia export; nominal/high-confidence detections on mainland Sumatra and Indonesian Kalimantan, filtered with Natural Earth land polygons. Counts are satellite detections, not fire totals or clusters, and are not directly comparable to ASMC’s NOAA-20 counts. Clouds can hide fires. No automatic hotspot updates are available in this standalone page.

open_in_new NEA Haze Information

HazeWatchSG · Independent air quality information — not operated or endorsed by NEA, MSS, MOH, ASMC or NASA. Local wind readings are not regional smoke forecasts.

Contains information from NEA’s PM2.5, PSI, Wind Direction and Wind Speed datasets accessed through data.gov.sg, made available under the Singapore Open Data Licence v1.0. Source observation times are shown with each feed; “Checked” records this page’s retrieval attempt.

Hotspot data: NASA FIRMS Suomi-NPP VIIRS 375 m, Collection 2 near-real-time rolling 24-hour export, downloaded 07 Oct 2026, 17:19 SGT. NASA source: FIRMS active-fire downloads. NASA data-use guidance. Singapore map image: Seloloving / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 (image unchanged, reading overlays added; map presentation under the same licence). Regional base-map coastlines: Natural Earth, public domain. Map boundaries are geographic references, not authoritative survey boundaries.

Privacy: this page has no accounts, subscriptions or analytics. Your preferred region is stored only in this browser. Your browser requests public readings from data.gov.sg and may contact Google Fonts; those providers and your hosting service may process request metadata under their own policies. No precise location is requested.

Readings may be delayed, revised or unavailable. This independent summary is general information, not personalised medical advice. Use current NEA readings and activity guidance for decisions. © 2026 HazeWatchSG; third-party data retains its applicable licence.

HAZEWATCHSG · READING GUIDE

Understanding your air quality

Selected readingAwaiting observationsNo observation

Use 1-hour PM2.5 for immediate outdoor activity decisions. For planning ahead, consult the official 24-hour PSI forecast and health advisory. These two scales are different and cannot be substituted for each other.

LowMidHigh

24-hour PSI classification thresholds
Index rangeCategory
0–50GoodCurrent

Colours are HazeWatchSG’s visual styling, not official NEA colour codes. Category names and thresholds remain unchanged. Health, symptoms, exposure duration and activity intensity also matter; a “Normal” PM2.5 band does not guarantee safety for every individual.
